_readme: Single source for the en/ site root (nav, SEO, catalog, sitemap). Human-readable fields are translation units tracked in i18n/ledger.json. Rebuild with: SITE_ROOT=en node scripts/build_nav.js

site.title: Home Assistant Onboarding Guide
site.subtitle: From zero to working
site.description: A 22-chapter Home Assistant guide with 3 appendices, covering login, areas, dashboards, notifications, automations, protocols, integrations, energy monitoring, historical data, voice assistants and LLMs, Docker architecture, and remote access. Each chapter takes about 10 minutes.
site.footerMeta: Screenshots show the official Home Assistant interface. Home Assistant is a trademark of the Open Home Foundation; this site is not affiliated with it.

hub._readme: index.html is an overview (hub) of four types of resources, which is maintained manually and is not touched by build_nav. The teaching catalog page is generated by build_nav to the file specified by catalog. Pages is an independent single-file manual under the hub (with its own head and style), which is included in the sitemap and check_links whitelist.

chapters.title: Log in to Home Assistant
chapters.card: Understand the differences between login pages, remember me, Companion App and web pages.
chapters.description: How to log in to Home Assistant: three ways to find the HA URL, the difference between Owner and Administrator, how to use “Stay logged in”, and the choice between the web backend and the Companion App.

chapters.title: System settings
chapters.card: Correct the time zone, language, unit, and geographical location once, and all subsequent automation will be accurate.
chapters.description: Home Assistant system setting tutorial: adjust the time zone, language, unit system and geographical location at once, so that automatic sunrise and sunset types will not calculate the wrong time.

chapters.title: Floors and areas
chapters.card: First draw the floors and rooms of your home, and then the controls, dashboard, and voice will be clear.
chapters.description: Create floors and areas in Home Assistant and put the devices in place so that dashboards, voice assistants, and automation can all be operated using “living room lights.”

chapters.title: Naming and labels
chapters.card: Turn “switch.0x00abc123” into the “living room main light” and use labels to group similar devices.
chapters.description: The difference between Home Assistant entity naming and entity_id design, Label label and Category classification, with a set of naming examples that can be copied directly.

chapters.title: User management
chapters.card: Create accounts for family members, tenants, and guests, and decide who can change settings and who can only turn on lights.
chapters.description: What is the difference between Home Assistant’s Users and Persons, how to open family and guest permissions, MFA two-stage verification settings, and mobile phone positioning and Zone radius calibration.

chapters.title: Dashboards
chapters.card: Put the most commonly used lights, curtains, and air conditioners on the homepage, and your family will use them as soon as they are turned on.
chapters.description: Home Assistant dashboard editing tutorial: adding cards, multi-page configuration, how to choose the four View Types, and layout tips that your family will use as soon as they open it.

chapters.title: Notifications
chapters.card: Install the Companion App, bind your phone, and send the first notification.
chapters.description: Install the Home Assistant Companion App, bind the phone and send the first push notification, and then make notifications with actionable notifications as you progress.

chapters.title: Your first automation
chapters.card: The three-stage trigger/condition/action avoids the device_id trap and writes “turn on the lights at sunset”.
chapters.description: Use the three-part trigger/condition/action to write the first Home Assistant automation “turn on the lights at sunset”, and explain why you should avoid device_id and use entity_id instead, with execution mode and Blueprint instructions.

chapters.title: backups
chapters.card: Set up automatic backup in 3 minutes, and then you can safely try out integrations and change settings.
chapters.description: Home Assistant backup tutorial: manually create a backup, enable automatic backup schedule, where to store the backup, and the steps for two restore scenarios.

chapters.title: Scripts
chapters.card: Packing repeated actions into a button is more flexible than automation and can be called with parameters.
chapters.description: Home Assistant Script script tutorial: differences with automation, Fields parameterization, Single/Restart/Queued/Parallel execution modes, and four entrances to call scripts.

chapters.title: Device settings
chapters.card: How to view the device page, how to upgrade the firmware, how to deactivate the entity, and how to save the repair center.
chapters.description: Understand the Home Assistant device page: renaming devices and entities, the difference between disabling/hiding/deleting, firmware updates, diagnostic downloads and repair centers (Repairs).

chapters.title: Domain reference
chapters.card: light / climate / cover / media_player… The common actions, UI cards, and common pitfalls of each Domain will be discussed in one go.
chapters.description: Home Assistant Domain control illustration: common actions, UI cards and common pitfalls of light, switch, climate, cover, media_player, lock, vacuum, fan, camera, sensor, notify.

chapters.title: Themes and appearance
chapters.card: Dark mode, social theme, everyone has their own style, and adjust the interface to how you want to live in it.
chapters.description: Home Assistant theme and appearance tutorial: dark and light mode, installing community themes through HACS, applying different themes to each user, changing the theme of the dashboard on a single page, as well as theme variables and brand customization.

chapters.title: Integrations
chapters.card: Weather, music, positioning, calendar - only when outside services are brought in, will the home know what is happening outside.
chapters.description: Home Assistant integration (Integration) tutorial: the complete process of new integration, the connection of weather and music with cloud services such as positioning and calendar, the choice between local integration and cloud integration, as well as diagnosis and removal.

chapters.title: Communication protocols
chapters.card: Wi-Fi / Zigbee / Z-Wave / Matter / KNX / Modbus will be explained in one go. Read this chapter before buying the equipment.
chapters.description: A complete comparison of Home Assistant communication protocols: differences between Wi-Fi, Zigbee, Z-Wave, Thread and Matter, Bluetooth, KNX, Modbus, and MQTT, purchasing recommendations, and integration methods in HA.

chapters.title: To-do lists and calendars
chapters.card: Take out the trash, pay the bill, change the filter - let the home remember what to do and remind you at the right time.
chapters.description: Home Assistant to-do list and calendar tutorial: Local To-do and shopping list, local calendar and Google calendar connection, dashboard cards, and using calendar events to trigger automation.

chapters.title: Energy dashboard and ESG practices
chapters.card: Turn electricity bills into understandable charts, find out the electricity-hungry monsters in your home, and make ESG reports.
chapters.description: Home Assistant energy dashboard setting tutorial: which sensor is needed, using Riemann sum and Utility Meter to convert power into electricity consumption, electricity price and cost tracking, and electricity consumption baseline and energy saving analysis.

chapters.title: History, Recorder, and data export
chapters.card: Where does the data exist, how long it can be stored, how to download it to CSV, and why your HA is running slower and slower.
chapters.description: Home Assistant historical data tutorial: the difference between History and Logbook, Recorder retention days and exclusion settings, long-term statistics, downloading CSV, and advanced practices of MariaDB and InfluxDB Grafana.

chapters.title: Voice assistants and LLM integration
chapters.card: From “turning on the lights in the living room” to talking to AI to manage your home, both local and cloud approaches are available.
chapters.description: Home Assistant voice assistant tutorial: Assist and conversational agents, local cloud solutions for wake words and speech-to-text, connecting to OpenAI or other LLMs as conversational agents, and privacy and cost trade-offs.

chapters.title: Add-ons and Docker architecture
chapters.card: Add-on is actually a Docker container. Only after understanding this layer can you understand why HA is so long.
chapters.description: Tutorial on Home Assistant Add-on and Docker architecture: the differences between the four installation methods, the role of Supervisor, a tour of must-install add-ons, automatic uploading of backups to the cloud, and a vernacular version of the core concepts of containers.

chapters.title: Networking and remote access
chapters.card: Fixed IP, reverse proxy, Cloudflare Tunnel, VPN—connect home securely even when you’re outside.
chapters.description: Home Assistant remote connection practice: DHCP fixed address, implementation of four routes of Nabu Casa and Cloudflare Tunnel, VPN and DDNS reverse proxy, trusted_proxies settings and information security hard rules.

chapters.title: Life logging and custom dashboards
chapters.card: Drinking water, keeping accounts, changing filters, family message boards - turn daily chores into a system that can draw its own diagrams.
chapters.description: Use Home Assistant auxiliary components to record your life: habit tracking, household income and expenses, equipment maintenance reminders and message boards, and use statistical charts, condition cards and Sections layout to create customized dashboards.

appendices.title: Ecosystem: HACS, add-ons, and remote access
appendices.pagerTitle: Ecosystem: HACS, add-ons, and remote access
appendices.card: Comparison of official add-ons, community kit store, and four external connection solutions. Come back after installing the main line.
appendices.description: Home Assistant ecosystem: official Add-on store, HACS community suite store, and comparison of four remote connection solutions: Nabu Casa, DDNS, VPN, and Cloudflare Tunnel.

appendices.title: Scenes, helpers, and groups
appendices.card: Scene, 10 types of Helper, and Group are three advanced weapons, making your home like a small program.
appendices.description: Home Assistant advanced three-piece set: Scene, 10 kinds of Helper auxiliary components and Group usage and matching examples, making the smart home look like a small program.

appendices.title: Before installation: hardware and HAOS
appendices.card: Don’t have a host yet? Read this first. How to choose hardware, how to burn HAOS, and what to set when booting for the first time.
appendices.description: Home Assistant installation prequel: Comparison of four installation methods, HAOS vs. Supervised vs. Container vs. Core, hardware selection such as Raspberry Pi vs. mini computer, SD card vs. SSD, image file burning steps, and first-time boot settings.
